\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آنها} (ânhâ)}{آنها (ânhâ)}]{\fa{آنها} (ânhâ) — those, they}

\label{lesson:FA-C83-anha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for that, then the Persian for these.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آنها}}
\textbf{\fa{آنها}} — \emph{ânhâ} — \textquotedblleft{}those, they\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ânhâ} is \emph{ân}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}, with the plural ending \emph{-hâ}: \textquotedblleft{}those\textquotedblright{}. Both pieces are native Persian; \emph{ân} is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{ān}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ânhâ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ânhâ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ânhâ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for that, then the Persian for these, then say \emph{ânhâ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{آنها} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Those, they\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
